subject: The pericardium
object: a protective fluid-filled sac around the heart. Its inflammation is called pericarditis and causes chest pain. Blood or fluid can leak into the sac when it is inflamed.
source: NHS website: Pericarditis
source_quote: Pericarditis is inflammation of the lining around your heart, which causes chest pain. Your heart has a protective fluid-filled sac around it called the pericardium. In pericarditis, the pericardium gets inflamed, and blood or fluid can leak into it.

subject: Pericardial involvement
object: autoimmune disorders such as systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjögren's syndrome, systemic sclerosis and vasculitis, and in organ-specific disorders such as inflammatory bowel disease. In autoimmune disorders, its forms include acute, recurrent, incessant, chronic and constrictive pericarditis, asymptomatic pericardial effusion and, rarely, cardiac tamponade. Pericardial symptoms sometimes appear before other systemic manifestations are present.
source: Article: Wassif H, Ghandakly E, Layoun H et al. Autoimmune Pericarditis: Diagnosis and New Therapeutics. Current Cardiology Reports 2025
source_quote: Moreover, pericardial involvement extends to other auto-immune disorders such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), Sjogren’s syndrome, systemic sclerosis, and vasculitis, in addition to organ-specific diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease . The clinical spectrum of pericardial involvement in autoimmune disorders includes acute, recurrent, incessant, chronic pericarditis and constrictive pericarditis, asymptomatic pericardial effusion, and rarely cardiac tamponade . In some cases, pericardial symptoms herald the presentation of disease, in the absence of other systemic manifestations.

subject: Acute pericarditis
object: a heterogeneous condition involving inflammation of the pericardium. The inflammatory response is typically mediated by innate immunity, with neutrophils and macrophages playing significant roles.
source: Article: Wassif H, Ghandakly E, Layoun H et al. Autoimmune Pericarditis: Diagnosis and New Therapeutics. Current Cardiology Reports 2025
source_quote: Acute pericarditis is a heterogeneous condition characterized by inflammation of the pericardium. The pathophysiology involves an inflammatory response, typically mediated by the innate immune system, with neutrophils and macrophages playing significant roles.

subject: The main symptom of pericarditis
object: chest pain. It usually feels sharp or stabbing, spreads to the shoulders, arms or tummy, worsens with deep breaths, swallowing, coughing or lying down, especially on the left side, and improves on leaning forward.
source: NHS website: Pericarditis
source_quote: The main symptom of pericarditis is chest pain. The chest pain usually: feels sharp or stabbing spreads to your shoulders, arms or tummy gets worse when you breathe in deeply, swallow, cough or lie down (especially when you lie down on your left side) gets better when you lean forward

subject: In a study of 471 patients with pericarditis, 7% of whom had autoimmune disease, people under 75
object: chest pain, pericardial rubs and widespread ST elevation. In patients over 75, breathlessness and pericardial and pleural effusions were more common.
source: Article: Wassif H, Ghandakly E, Layoun H et al. Autoimmune Pericarditis: Diagnosis and New Therapeutics. Current Cardiology Reports 2025
source_quote: A recent study of 471 patients, of which 7% were noted to have autoimmune disease, described in detail the variation of presentation in patients under the age of 75 years compared to over 75 years (geriatric group). Younger patients presented more frequently with chest pain, pericardial rubs, widespread ST- segment elevation, while the geriatric group depicted more commonly dyspnea, pericardial and pleural effusion .

subject: Transthoracic echocardiography
relation: is the first-line imaging test for
object: pericardial disease because it is widely available and low in cost. Echocardiography is key to assessing effusion size and signs of constrictive physiology.
source: Article: Wassif H, Ghandakly E, Layoun H et al. Autoimmune Pericarditis: Diagnosis and New Therapeutics. Current Cardiology Reports 2025
source_quote: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) remains the first line in diagnosis imaging of pericardial disease due to its widespread availability and low cost. Echo evaluation is key to determine the size of the effusion as well as the hallmarks of constrictive physiology.

subject: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
object: of increasing value in diagnosing and managing pericardial disease. T2-STIR signal and late gadolinium enhancement are typically increased in the acute phase. In the chronic phase the increased T2-STIR signal disappears, and late gadolinium enhancement correlates with severity and outcomes.
source: Article: Wassif H, Ghandakly E, Layoun H et al. Autoimmune Pericarditis: Diagnosis and New Therapeutics. Current Cardiology Reports 2025
source_quote: CMR offers a comprehensive second-line modality and has increasingly rendered its value in the diagnosis and management of pericardial disease. In the acute phase, there is typically increased signal in both T2-STIR and LGE. In the chronic phase, the former disappears, and the latter is correlated with severity and outcomes.

object: additional treatment. A GP may prescribe colchicine if anti-inflammatory painkillers are ineffective or pericarditis keeps recurring, steroids if colchicine is ineffective, or antibiotics if a bacterial infection is the cause.

source_quote: You may need other treatment. For example, a GP may prescribe medicines such as: colchicine – if anti-inflammatory painkillers do not work or pericarditis keeps coming back steroids – if colchicine does not work antibiotics – if pericarditis is caused by a bacterial infection

subject: Recurrent pericarditis

subject: A nationwide Japanese cohort of 20,000 hospitalised patients with pericarditis
object: rates of cardiac tamponade in autoimmune pericarditis. In patients with autoimmune pericarditis, systemic lupus erythematosus was the diagnosis most commonly associated with tamponade, followed by rheumatoid arthritis and systemic sclerosis.
source: Article: Wassif H, Ghandakly E, Layoun H et al. Autoimmune Pericarditis: Diagnosis and New Therapeutics. Current Cardiology Reports 2025
source_quote: A recent nationwide Japanese cohort of 20,000 hospitalized patients with pericarditis sought to investigate the rates of cardiac tamponade in AAP. Among patients with AAP, SLE was the most common diagnosis associated with cardiac tamponade complications, followed by rheumatoid arthritis and systemic sclerosis .

subject: In constrictive pericardial disease, constrictive physiology
object: dissociation of intrathoracic and intracardiac pressures during respiration, and ventricular interdependence with raised diastolic filling pressure in both right- and left-sided chambers.
source: Article: Wassif H, Ghandakly E, Layoun H et al. Autoimmune Pericarditis: Diagnosis and New Therapeutics. Current Cardiology Reports 2025
source_quote: Echocardiography Constrictive physiology involves two unique features:1) dissociation between intrathoracic and intracardiac pressure with respiration; and 2) interventricular dependance with increased diastolic filling pressure in both right- and left-sided chambers.
